gd.adv.li1: Use current action settings — Starts with the main order · Per turn cells · exception turns as they are.
gd.adv.li2: Defaults — Resets the action plan to the role default rhythm and starts from there (can be undone).
gd.adv.li3: Resume previous — Appears when saved advanced settings exist, and loads the last advanced settings.
gd.adv.note1: Advanced settings turn on automatically when you turn on the escape room altar or load a record or share code containing Advanced settings values. While the altar is on, Advanced settings can't be turned off, and the main action plan shows ‘The altar is on, so edit in Advanced settings only’.
gd.adv.p1: Press Edit detailed actions in Advanced settings at the bottom of the action plan to open the window. It has four parts: ① Order and EX Skill · ② Exception Turns · ③ EX Skill Link · ④ Turn-by-Turn Action Plan. Turn on the Use advanced settings switch at the top for them to be used in runs.
gd.adv.p2: Turning the switch on asks how to start. While in use, the main action plan is locked and all actions are edited in this window. When you turn it off, the EX Skill modes · Assume success · EX Skill links · locked turns set here are kept, and runs use only the main settings.
gd.adv.title: Advanced Settings
gd.ally.p1: When Xuying is on the team, Xuying's row has an Ally EX Skill later checkbox. When on, adjacent companions use their EX Skill in the extra action granted after Xuying's EX Skill; when off, adjacent companions use their EX Skill first and the granted extra action is a Normal Attack. It is the same setting as the Xuying preset in Advanced settings ③.
gd.ally.p2: When Lee Taeho is in slot 1 and Boss Ren is on the team, setting Lee Taeho to Per turn adds Extra action granted by Boss Ren cells under the row, so you can set that action for each turn.
gd.ally.title: Xuying · Lee Taeho
gd.altar.li1: For the Star Altar, the penalties of unlit altars apply to the battle; for the Moon Altar, the buffs of lit altars apply. By default everything is lit (no penalties · all buffs).
gd.altar.li2: Floors can only be used in order from floor 1, and turning on an upper floor also turns on the floors below. When the same effect is on several floors, they all add up.
gd.altar.li3: The Boss ATK · boss damage dealt · ally damage taken Star Altars only affect results when Incoming Damage is on.
gd.altar.li4: Turning on the altar turns off Always proc, and the two can't be used together.
gd.altar.li5: Turning on the altar automatically turns on Advanced settings, and while the altar is on, the action plan is edited only in Advanced settings.
gd.altar.note1: When the ‘Chance CD cut’ altar is lit, EX Skill turns can vary from run to run. To see the planned turns, use Assume success in Advanced settings ①; to see real probabilities, use As soon as ready.
gd.altar.p1: Applies the guild escape room altar effects to the battle. Turn on Use altar effects and choose floors and altars in Set lit altars by floor.
gd.altar.title: Escape Room Altars
gd.assist.li1: Assume success for all — The button next to the notice turns it on or off for all eligible companions at once.
gd.assist.li2: For ‘As soon as ready’ companions, companions with a once-per-battle EX Skill, or when the altar is off, the checkbox is dimmed and the reason is shown.
gd.assist.li3: The result header also shows the probability that the flow calculated with Assume success actually happens.
gd.assist.note1: To see the flow that uses the EX Skill whenever it is ready under real probabilities, use ‘As soon as ready’ instead of Assume success.
gd.assist.p1: When the escape room altar's ‘Chance CD cut’ effect is lit, a notice appears at the top of the window and each companion row gets an Assume success checkbox. When on, no chance is rolled; only as many successes as the EX Skill turns need are counted, so you can plan EX Skills on turns the base cooldown can't reach (e.g. turns 3 · 6 · 9 for a companion with a 3-turn CD).
gd.assist.title: Assume Success
gd.cell.li1: Pick one of Normal Attack · EX Skill · Defend. The current action is marked.
gd.cell.li2: On turns where the cooldown hasn't come back, the EX Skill can't be picked and the reason is shown under the item. Turns blocked by Boss Ren's CD change immunity show that reason separately.
gd.cell.li3: For companions whose EX Skill CD drops when they defend (Moyru · Watanabe Hitoha), picking an EX Skill cell automatically places Defend on the turns needed before it, and an impossible turn tells you why. For Zetto, whose EX Skill is once per battle, EX Skills set on other turns are cleared.
gd.cell.p1: Tapping a cell in the Per turn row opens a small picker for that turn's action (a sheet from the bottom on phones). With the keyboard, move with the up/down arrows, confirm with Enter, and close with Esc.
gd.cell.title: Picking a Cell
gd.compare.li1: Team selection — Pick a record for Team A · B and it is calculated right away.
gd.compare.li2: Common Battle Settings — Turns (by default the shorter of the two records) · Always proc · enemy HP 10% · enemy element · enemy count · ally hits taken · incoming damage. Escape room altars and turn damage apply the main settings to both teams.
gd.compare.li3: Companion matchup — Pairs the same companions and shows the damage difference. Tap a cell to swap · remove a companion, and fill slots with Add companion.
gd.compare.li4: Per-team actions — Edit action plan opens that team's own Advanced settings window, and Action order opens order editing. After editing, recalculate with Compare.
gd.compare.li5: Cumulative dmg per turn — The two teams' cumulative curves overlap; hover to see that turn's values and the difference.
gd.compare.p1: Open it with Team comparison at the top. Two saved records (or teams you build yourself from an empty lineup) are run side by side under the same conditions and compared. Team · condition changes made in the comparison screen are not applied to the main screen.
gd.compare.title: Team Comparison
gd.cond.li1: Iterations — 1–200 (default 50). Because of chance effects, the battle is run many times and the median is taken. More is more accurate but slower.
gd.cond.li2: Turns — 1–30. The number of cells in the action plan follows this value too.
gd.cond.li3: Always proc — Calculates every chance-based trigger · buff at 100%. Runs only once, without iterations.
gd.cond.li4: 10% HP mode — Fixes enemy HP at 10% so that all low-HP conditional effects (Capt. Locke etc.) trigger.
gd.cond.li5: Dummy Element · Enemy Dummies — An advantaged element is ×1.5 and a disadvantaged one ×0.75; no element or an unrelated element has no effect. The enemy count is 1–5.
gd.cond.li6: Ally Hits Taken — 0 (no attacks), 1~5 (N random allies are each attacked), All (all allies are attacked once at the same time). This changes results such as the number of counterattacks.
gd.cond.li7: Incoming Damage — When on, enemy attacks deal the set % of allies' max HP as damage. Barriers absorb it first, and an ally dies when HP reaches 0.
gd.cond.p1: Set the battle environment in the right panel. Changed items are marked, and you can revert with each group's Default or Reset all in the header.
gd.cond.title: Battle Conditions
gd.contrib.p1: Each companion's direct share of the total damage and its percentage. Companions who provided healing · barriers also show those amounts.
gd.contrib.title: Damage by Companion
gd.end.note1: Not every companion has been verified, and some companions' passives may be handled incorrectly. If you find an error or something to improve, please let us know via Feedback in the ≡ menu.
gd.exc.p1: Uses a different action order on specific turns only. Press Add turns to pick several turns and set their order; it applies to all the chosen turns at once (e.g. a different order on turns 4 · 7 · 10 only). Only the order changes; actions follow the rules. Turns with a dot already have an exception.
gd.exc.title: ② Exception Turns
gd.exc2.p1: The same as the main plan's exception turns. Tapping a turn number in ④ and changing only the order gives the same setting.
gd.exc2.title: ② Exception Turns
gd.fig.team-chips: Chips for items that differ from max build
gd.grid.li1: Tap a cell — Pin Normal Attack · EX Skill · Defend, or choose Unpin (follow rules). The same menu has Edit this turn and Lock this turn (as it runs now). You can't pin the EX Skill on a turn where the cooldown hasn't come back (possible with Assume success on).
gd.grid.li2: Tap a companion name — Apply All EX Skill or a companion preset to that row, or choose Clear all pins in this row.
gd.grid.li3: Tap a turn number — Opens the edit window for that turn.
gd.grid.li4: Undo · Clear all pins · Lock all turns — Tools at the top right of the grid. The ⓘ next to them summarizes the priority.
gd.grid.p1: A turns × 5-member grid shows in color the actions that will actually run. Pin actions only on the cells you want; the remaining cells follow the EX Skill mode in ① and the EX Skill links in ③.
gd.grid.title: ④ Turn-by-Turn Action Plan
gd.grow.li1: Level — 1–60. Has the largest effect on stats.
gd.grow.li2: Star — 0–5. Determines skill unlocks; when you lower it, the skills that become locked are marked in the skill level list.
gd.grow.li3: Evolution phase — The phase within a Star. Its cap depends on the Star (Star 2 → 0–14), and at Star 5 there are no further phases, so it is disabled.
gd.grow.li5: Unlock Sigil — When on, the Sigil EX Skill is used; when off, the regular EX Skill. Available from Star 3.
gd.grow.note1: Star determines skill unlocks. Passive 2 can be leveled from Star 2 (fixed at level 1 before that), Star 3 unlocks Passive 3 and the Sigil, and Star 4 · 5 unlock Passive 4 · 5 in turn. Locked skills are marked ‘Unlocks at Star N’ and do not trigger.
gd.grow.p1: Tap the portrait on a team card to open the build window. The header shows the ATK · HP calculated with the current settings and the % of max build; below are the build, Sigil boost, and skill levels. Changes apply immediately.
gd.grow.p2: Turn on Use build settings to change values. When off, calculations use max build (Lv60 · Star 5 · Compatibility 5 · all skill levels 10 · Sigil unlocked).
gd.grow.p3: Skill levels set Normal Attack · EX Skill · Passives 1–5 to 1–10 each, and each row shows the skill description at that level. Turning on Sigil boost lets you split the companion's boost limit between ATK and HP (raising one lowers the other). Reset to default returns the build, Sigil, and boost to max build.
gd.grow.p4: Companions that differ from max build get chips under their team card showing the difference (e.g. ★3 · Lv50 · Compatibility 2), so you can see at a glance which companions are not at max build.
gd.grow.title: Companion Build
gd.hero.p1: The big number is the median of the iterated results. The bar below spans from no chance effects triggering to all of them triggering, and the dot marks the median. The narrower it is, the less the team depends on chance. Damage per turn and the chance spread (±%) are shown alongside.
gd.hero.title: Total Damage · Chance Range
gd.imm.li1: The immunity lasts for the rest of the turn in which Boss Ren used the EX Skill and the next two turns.
gd.imm.li2: During immunity, CD cuts from Defend, altars, and skills, as well as Assume success credits for the chance CD cut, do not apply. The CD resetting to its maximum after an EX Skill and the natural recharge of 1 per turn still apply.
gd.imm.li3: If Boss Ren uses the EX Skill again during immunity, the CD −3 is blocked and only the immunity duration is renewed. Cells where the EX Skill can't be used because of immunity show that reason, and the battle log records it as ‘nullified by CD change immunity’.
gd.imm.p1: Boss Ren's EX Skill cuts the slot-1 companion's EX Skill CD by 3 and grants that companion CD change immunity for 3 turns. The action plan, preview, and runs all follow this rule.
gd.imm.title: Boss Ren's CD Change Immunity
gd.intro: XXL WOOFIA is a game built around the synergy of a 5-member team. This simulator lets you build the team, builds, and action plan yourself and see the damage as numbers. Set up the team and action plan on the left, then press Run Simulation under the battle conditions on the right, and the results appear below. The top bar holds History · Team Comparison · Lounge · the ≡ menu.
gd.log.li1: Action cards — Companion · action type (EX Skill · Normal Attack · Defend · Passive · damage over time) · number of hits · total. Expand to see the target and value of each hit.
gd.log.li2: Calculation — Expand a hit to break it down into ATK total × skill multiplier × damage dealt × damage taken … = final formula and per-step bars.
gd.log.li3: Source — Expand each step to see the companions · skills · conditions that produced the value, with their shares. Tap a skill name to open its description.
gd.log.li4: Effects · Damage Taken — Records healing · barriers · buffs · debuffs · stacks · cooldown changes, plus barrier absorption · HP loss from enemy attacks · turn damage.
gd.log.note1: The log's calculations are the exact formulas the engine used. If the multiplied value differs from the engine result, it shows up as an ‘Unexplained difference’ row; if you find one, please let us know via feedback.
gd.log.p1: Shows, turn by turn, the one run whose total damage is closest to the average. Pick a turn on the left and that turn's actions appear in order on the right.
gd.log.title: Battle Log
gd.lounge.li1: Share to Lounge — The button in the result header posts the current team to the Lounge's team sharing.
gd.lounge.li2: See comments — The button in the companion build window header opens Lounge comments about that companion.
gd.lounge.li3: Opening the simulator from a team link sent from the Lounge loads that team and tells you in a notification.
gd.lounge.p1: The XXL Lounge gathers companion comments · tier lists · team sharing. Lounge in the top bar takes you there in the same tab.
gd.lounge.title: XXL Lounge

gd.mode.li1: Auto — The role default rhythm. A missed EX Skill is used as soon as it is ready.
gd.mode.li2: Planned turns only — Used only on the default turns and pinned cells. If it isn't ready on that turn, it is skipped.
gd.mode.li3: As soon as ready — Used the moment the cooldown comes back. In this mode the EX Skill takes precedence over pinned Normal Attacks, so the 3-turn presets are shown dimmed.
gd.mode.p1: Order editing is the same as in the main plan, and there are three EX Skill modes. Cells not pinned in ④ are filled according to this mode.
gd.mode.p2: Checkboxes under a row appear only when they have an effect. Keep Def turns (on by default) makes ‘As soon as ready’ companions and EX Skill link members defend on their pinned Defend cells even when the EX Skill is ready. Assume success is explained in the next section.
gd.mode.title: ① Order and EX Skill Mode
gd.nav.li1: History — Pick a saved record to switch to its team and conditions.
gd.nav.li2: Team Comparison — Runs two teams side by side under the same conditions.
gd.nav.li4: ≡ menu — Records · Guide · Patch History · Feedback · Classic version, plus language · theme.
gd.nav.p1: The top bar stays fixed at the top of the screen while you scroll. Tap the logo to go back to the top.

gd.order.li1: Auto — Uses the EX Skill on the default rhythm for the role. The selector shows the EX Skill turns (e.g. Auto · turns 4·7·10).
gd.order.li2: Per turn — Opens a row of turn cells under the row, plus the preset buttons that fit that companion. Turns you don't set follow the role default rhythm.
gd.order.p1: The row order is the action order within a turn. Drag rows or use ↑↓ to change it (on phones, long-press then drag). The default order is by position (Support → Vandal → Healer → Tank → Fighter), and companions that must act after allies, like Boss Ren, go to the back. Pick the EX Skill mode in each row's selector.
gd.order.p2: Switching Per turn back to Auto clears all of that companion's set cells. You can cancel it with Undo in the notification.
gd.order.title: ① Order and EX Skill
gd.plan.p1: Decide who acts first within a turn and who uses the EX Skill when. Even in the same turn, buff and combo results change with the action order. The action plan has two parts, ① Order and EX Skill · ② Exception Turns, and the Run preview at the bottom shows the current settings as a turn grid. Finer settings open from Edit detailed actions in Advanced settings at the bottom.
gd.plan.title: Action Plan
gd.preset.li1: EX Skill every 3 turns — EX Skill on turns 4 · 7 · 10…, Normal Attack otherwise (Invisible Man · Oyamada Mataya).
gd.preset.li2: Passive Def — Defend on the turn right before each EX Skill (Famido · Souran).
gd.preset.li3: Every 3 turns · Def before — EX Skill every 3 turns, with Defend on the turn right before it (Souran).
gd.preset.li4: Pull EX Skill forward with Def — Cuts the CD by defending and uses the EX Skill on the earliest possible turns (Moyru · Watanabe Hitoha).
gd.preset.li5: Re-space EX Skills — Keeps the first EX Skill and re-places the later ones on each turn the cooldown comes back.
gd.preset.note1: Applying a preset shows Undo in the notification. Souran's Defend effect triggers only when the position-4 companion acts after Souran, and Moyru must act after the allies for that turn's Normal Attacks to count toward the CD cut.
gd.preset.p1: The buttons above the Per turn row fill the turn cells at once. Only the buttons that fit the companion appear, and each button's description shows the companion's skill basis.
gd.preset.title: Companion Presets
gd.preview.li1: Order only — back to the default order
gd.preview.li2: Exception turns only — deletes all exception turns
gd.preview.li3: Per-turn plans only — clears the set cells of all companions

gd.preview.p1: The actions from one run of the current settings, assuming every chance effect triggers. Rows follow the action order and cells are turns. Point at a cell to see that turn's action; when you change settings, the changed cells are highlighted briefly.
gd.preview.p2: Choose what to revert with Reset in the header. Every reset can be canceled with Undo in the notification.
gd.preview.title: Run Preview · Reset
gd.prio.li1: Locked turn — That turn runs exactly as its list, and EX Skill links · pinned cells · exception turns don't apply.
gd.prio.p1: When several settings overlap on the same cell, the one higher in this list wins.
gd.prio.p2: In the grid, cells where the pin and the actual run differ get an orange dot (Runs differently), and pinned cells covered by a locked turn are shown as Hidden pin. Point at a cell to see what decided it (locked turn · EX Skill link · order and EX Skill mode · pinned cell · exception turn).

gd.sync.li1: EX Skill before / EX Skill after — Uses the EX Skill together, right before or after the lead.
gd.sync.li2: Defend → EX Skill in the granted extra action / Normal Attack → EX Skill in the granted extra action — Defends (or uses a Normal Attack) on that turn, then uses the EX Skill in the extra action granted by the lead's EX Skill. Extra actions go only to allies who have already acted, so this companion acts before the lead.
gd.sync.li3: Other turns — The action on turns where the lead doesn't use the EX Skill. Choose Save the EX Skill or Use my own policy; ‘EX Skill in the granted extra action’ companions default to Use my own policy.
gd.sync.li4: If the lead isn't ready — Choose whether to wait for the next EX Skill or use it as soon as ready.
gd.sync.note1: When a companion whose EX Skill resets allies' cooldowns and its target both receive extra actions on the same turn, the target with its EX Skill ready acts first. After using its EX Skill, the target gets its cooldown back and can use the EX Skill once more that turn.
gd.sync.p1: Aligns the actions of the Members to the turns where the Lead uses the EX Skill. There are up to 3 groups, and a companion can be in only one group. Members have four actions.
gd.sync.p2: When Xuying is on the team, the Link adjacent companions to Xuying button binds the companions on both sides as ‘Normal Attack → EX Skill in the granted extra action’ at once. It is the same setting as the ‘Ally EX Skill later’ checkbox in the main action plan, and if a Xuying-led group already exists, it asks before overwriting.

gd.tdmg.li1: Barriers absorb it first, defending turns take only half, and damage-taken modifiers apply. Counterattacks do not trigger.
gd.tdmg.li2: When HP reaches 0 the ally dies and is removed from later actions · hits · buffs. With a revival effect such as Kyrian's Sigil, the ally can come back.
gd.tdmg.li3: Vary by turn sets the number of allies hit (1–4 · All; if fewer than all, allies with the highest current HP% first) and a different % per turn. Empty cells use the default.
gd.tdmg.p1: Turn on Turn Dmg in the damage-taken group, and at the end of each enemy phase allies take the set % of their max HP as damage. Use it to check companions that react to their own HP (Mumei etc.) and the value of healing · revival.

gd.team.li1: Choose a slot — Tap an empty slot first to make it the target; the next companion you pick goes into that slot.
gd.team.li2: Remove · Swap — Remove with the × at the card's top right. Drag a card onto another slot to swap the two companions (on phones, long-press then drag; on keyboard, Alt+arrow keys). Exception turns, pinned cells, and EX Skill links move along with them.
gd.team.li3: Search · Filter — Narrow the list by name search, element (Fire · Water · Wood · Light · Dark), and position (Fighter · Tank · Healer · Support · Vandal).

guide.section.adv.body: Press the ‘Advanced Action Setup’ button next to Action Priority to open it. There are three tabs — Turn timeline (set who acts, in what order and with what action, turn by turn), EX Skill policy (when each companion uses its EX Skill) and Sync (align other companions' actions to one companion's EX Skill turn). Only the Turn timeline tab has an ‘Enable’ switch; the other two tabs always apply.
guide.section.adv.body10: Press a companion chip to add an action to that turn. Companions with no action budget left do not show a chip.
guide.section.adv.body2: It applies only when “Use” at the top right of the Turn timeline tab is on. The moment it is on, Action Priority, Per-turn override and Per-turn Action Plan are all replaced by this screen and locked. Turning it off restores the original settings, and what you built here is not erased by toggling. The first time you turn it on it starts from the default setup, independent of your existing settings.
guide.section.adv.body3: After copying, a clipboard row appears telling you which turn and how many actions it holds. Clear it with “Clear”.
guide.section.adv.body4: Pick the turn to edit. Turns that differ from the default get a dot at the top right. In the image above, turns 4, 7, 10, 13, 16, 19, 22, 25 and 28 are selected and outlined. Selecting several turns applies Paste and Reset to all of them.
guide.section.adv.body5: The selected turns are listed as they are; clear them with “Clear selection”.
guide.section.adv.body6: Pressing “Overview” lays out every turn as a table. Dot colours mean Basic Attack, EX Skill and Defend; several dots in one cell mean that companion acts multiple times that turn. Click a cell to edit just that companion’s action on that turn.
guide.section.adv.body7: The turn being edited and its total action count. “Reset this turn” restores only this turn.
guide.section.adv.body8: The number on the left is the execution order. On each row pick Basic / EX / Defend to change the action, move it with , and remove it with . The currently selected action is highlighted in yellow.
guide.section.adv.body9: A row tagged “Extra” is an action granted by an earlier EX Skill. The same companion can appear several times in one turn. Actions that cannot be used — like the EX Skill on row 10 in the image above — are disabled in advance so they cannot be chosen by mistake.
guide.section.adv.item: Copy · Paste — copies the whole arrangement of the current turn into another turn. Turns it cannot fit are rejected.
guide.section.adv.item2: Select all compatible turns — finds the turns the clipboard fits and only selects them. Nothing is applied until you press Paste, so you can check where it would land first. Build a 3-turn EX cycle on turn 4, press this, and turns 7, 10 and 13 are picked at once.
guide.section.adv.item3: Undo — undoes the last change one at a time. Order moves () are recorded too.
guide.section.adv.item4: Overview — opens a table showing every turn at a glance.
guide.section.adv.item5: Reset selected turns — resets the turns selected above all at once.
guide.section.adv.item6: Reset all turns — resets every turn to the default setup.
guide.section.adv.item7: Import current settings — imports the action plan, priority and per-turn order you have been using as a timeline. A good starting point for tweaking per-companion cycles.
guide.section.adv.note: The action budget is computed by the simulator. An action beyond the budget is not executed, and an EX Skill still on cooldown comes out as a Basic Attack. The list shows this, so the screen never disagrees with the actual result.
guide.section.adv.note2: In the compare window you can also build a separate timeline per group using the same button inside the Action Priority popup. When a group has this on, that companion’s Action row is locked.
guide.section.adv.title: Advanced Action Setup
guide.section.altar.body: Press ‘Guild Altar Settings’ to open the list of altar effects by floor. Turn on Useat the top right for it to affect the battle.
guide.section.altar.item: Star Altar — penalties from unlit altars (less healing received, higher max EX Skill CD, etc.) apply in battle. Moon Altar — buffs from lit altars apply in battle.
guide.section.altar.item2: Floors can be lit only in order from floor 1, and lighting an upper floor also lights the floors below. Each effect can be turned on or off individually.
guide.section.altar.title: Guild Altar Settings
guide.section.altarTdmg.body: The buttons in the Battle Settings header let you add the Guild Escape Room’s altar effectsand per-turn damageto the battle for testing. Both open as tabs in the same place (right panel), so only one shows at a time and they switch between each other.
guide.section.char.body: Selecting a companion opens its detail panel.
guide.section.char.item: Sigil Boost on/off and ATK / HP allocation
guide.section.char.item2: Companion Spec — set Star, Evolution Phase, Level, Compatibility and per-skill levels in the right panel. When off it uses fully invested (Lv60 · Star 5 · Compatibility 5 · all skills 10 · sigil unlocked), so leaving it off gives the same results as before.

guide.section.compare.item: The bottom-right of the site (above this Guide button), Compare Teams button opens the comparison window.
guide.section.compare.item2: Pick a group — load existing records, or build a team one companion at a time with the Add button
guide.section.compare.item3: Turn setting — auto-aligns to the shortest turn count among groups; editable
guide.section.compare.item4: Per-companion settings — set swap target, sigil boost, per-turn action and action priority per group
guide.section.compare.item5: Graph — shows both cumulative damage curves; hover to see the per-turn difference (value · %)

guide.section.cond.item2: Enemy HP fixed at 10% — for checking low-HP conditions
guide.section.cond.item3: Iterations — used to find the median. Higher is more accurate but slower
guide.section.cond.item5: Dummy Element — pick None·Fire·Water·Wood·Light·Dark to check advantage (×1.5) · disadvantage (×0.75) (None · neutral element: no effect)
guide.section.cond.item7: Ally Hits Taken — 0(allies are not hit), 1~5(N enemies hit individually), All(all allies hit once together). Counter count and other results change.

guide.section.grow.body: Press the “Companion Spec” button at the top right of Sigil Boost in the companion panel and a window opens beside the card. Star, Evolution Phase, Level, Compatibility and per-skill levels are set separately for each companion.
guide.section.grow.body2: While “Use” at the top right is off, everything is calculated as fully invested (Lv60 · Star 5 · Compatibility 5 · all skills 10 · sigil unlocked), just as before. Leaving it off changes nothing, and right after turning it on the values are still fully invested — so you only lower what you want.
guide.section.grow.body3: ATK and HP for the current setup are shown immediately and follow the sliders as you drag. The “vs fully invested %” on the right tells you at a glance how far you are from max. This value is the base figure before Sigil Boost is added.
guide.section.grow.body4: Moving the slider lights up the stars. It is the key value deciding which skills below are unlocked, so lowering it changes the locked skills in the skill list too.
guide.section.grow.body5: A phase within a star. Its cap depends on the star (4 at Star 0, 24 at Star 4), and Star 5 is disabled because there is no further phase. Mid-phase there are no unlocks — only stats rise.
guide.section.grow.body6: Level ranges 1–60 and has the largest effect on stats.
guide.section.grow.body7: Compatibility ranges 0–5 and hearts light up with the slider. It is disabled for rarities that have no bond bonus.
guide.section.grow.body8: Set Basic Attack, EX Skill and Passives to 1–10 each; skill names and icons are shown alongside. Turning on the “Unlock Sigil” switch just under the EX Skill uses the Sigil EX Skill, turning it off uses the normal one, and the right side states which will be used. This switch becomes available from Star 3.
guide.section.grow.body9: Passives are adjusted one by one as well. A skill locked by a low star shows “Star N” and does not trigger at all, while a skill that is unlocked but not yet levelable shows “Star N+” and is calculated at level 1.
guide.section.grow.note: Star decides skill unlocks. Star 2 opens leveling for Passive 2, Star 3 opens Passive 3 and the sigil, and Stars 4 and 5 open Passives 4 and 5 in turn. Basic Attack, EX Skill and Passive 1 can be adjusted from the start.
guide.section.grow.note2: A companion with spec on gets a star badge at the bottom left of its team slot, so non-fully-invested companions stand out at a glance. In the compare window, click a companion and use the “Spec” button next to “Swap” to open the same screen; giving each group a different spec lets you compare investment levels directly.
guide.section.grow.title: Companion Spec
guide.section.intro.intro: A simulator that calculates a 5-companion team's damage turn by turn.
guide.section.order.body: Since who moves first in a turn changes buff and combo results, you can set the action order yourself.
guide.section.order.item: By default the party’s action order is the same every turn; drag the list to reorder.
guide.section.order.item2: Per-turn override — toggle the turns you want to change and edit them at once; the new order applies only to the selected turns. (e.g., turns 4·7·10 only)
guide.section.order.item3: Reset all button resets the order at once.
guide.section.order.title: Action Priority
guide.section.records.body: Results are recorded automatically and can be found again by name search / sort. From the ⋮ menu of a record item, rename · pin · lock · delete are available.
guide.section.records.body2: Export / Import — save selected records (multiple allowed) to a file or copy as a share code; paste a received code into Import to load it.
guide.section.records.note: When you reload or reopen the page, the settings you were last working on come back as they were. Loading a record switches to that record’s team and conditions, and ‘Undo’ in the notice takes you back to the state before loading. Removing a companion and adding it back restores its settings (spec · plan · EX Skill policy · sync).
guide.section.records.note2: Not every companion is fully verified, and some passives may be handled incorrectly. If you find an error or improvement, feedback is welcome.
guide.section.stats.body: Shows total damage, DPS and turn count, plus a bar ranking of damage per companion. Each value comes with the median and the chance range (no chance effects trigger – all trigger).
guide.section.stats.title: Stats · Ranking
guide.section.sync.body: The third tab of Advanced Action Setup. On the turn the group’s leaduses its EX Skill, decide what the membersdo (up to 3 groups; a companion can be in only one group).
guide.section.sync.item: EX Skill together — uses the EX Skill together, right before or after the lead.
guide.section.sync.item2: Defend → EX Skill in the granted extra action / Attack → EX Skill in the granted extra action — defends (or attacks) on the lead’s EX Skill turn and uses its EX Skill in the extra action the lead’s EX Skill grants. Example: Mataya defends → Xuying EX Skill → Mataya EX Skill in the extra action. Extra actions only go to allies who already acted, so this member automatically acts before the lead.
guide.section.sync.item3: On turns the lead doesn’t use its EX Skill, each member chooses Save the EX Skill or Use my own policy. Members set to ‘EX Skill in the granted extra action’ default to their own policy, so they use the EX Skill whenever it is ready and only on the lead’s EX Skill turn switch to defend → EX Skill in the extra action.
guide.section.sync.item4: When a companion that refills an ally’s cooldown with its EX Skill and that ally both get extra actions in the same turn, the ally acts first if its EX Skill is ready. Its cooldown then comes back after it uses its EX Skill, so it can use the EX Skill once more that turn.
guide.section.sync.item5: With Xuying on the team, the sync preset button groups the adjacent allies in one click.
guide.section.sync.note: When the timeline is on it takes priority, so these two tabs are paused. The timeline tab also notes when ‘Per-turn order’ or ‘Per-companion turn plans’ remain unapplied, and ‘Import current settings’ moves them into the timeline.
guide.section.sync.title: Sync (EX Skill timing)
guide.section.tdmg.body: Every turn, all allies take damage equal to a fixed % of max HP. Use it to check companions that react to their own HP (Mumei, etc.) and the value of healers and revival.
guide.section.tdmg.item: Applied at the end of the enemy phase; barriers absorb it first, and a defending turn takes only half. Damage-taken modifiers also apply.
guide.section.tdmg.item2: At 0 HP the companion is knocked out and leaves the battle— excluded from further actions, hits and buffs (its damage stops). Incoming Damage mode works the same way, so whether a healer keeps HP up shows directly in the result.
guide.section.tdmg.item3: Revival — Kyrian’s sigil revives one fallen ally at 25% max HP with a chance when the EX Skill fires. Being chance-based, it is included in the variance band (floor–ceiling).
guide.section.tdmg.item4: Targets (number of allies) — choose how many allies (1–5) are hit each turn (default All). With fewer than all, the allies with the highest current HP% are hit first (ties random) — useful for reproducing an ally that was just healed becoming the next target.
guide.section.tdmg.item5: Advanced · per-turn valueslets you set the damage % for each turn separately. Empty cells use the default above.
guide.section.tdmg.title: Turn Damage Settings
guide.section.team.body: Build a 5-member party from the roster. The top-right X of an icon, or clicking it again in the roster, removes a companion.
guide.section.team.title: Team Setup
guide.section.trace.body: Traces every damage source to the end.
guide.section.trace.item: Shows damage source (skill · counter · passive) and links skill info
guide.section.trace.item2: Breaks down the damage formula (Base ATK · coefficient · flat · advantage, etc.)
guide.section.trace.title: Damage Tracing
guide.section.turnPlan.body: You can set each companion’s action (Basic Attack · EX Skill · Defend) per turn. When off it is handled automatically; special cases like 2-action companions have dedicated settings.
guide.section.turnPlan.note: Clicking a cell changes only that cell. Later EX Skills move along with the cooldown only when you click an EX Skill on the untouched default plan; use ‘Re-space EX’ to re-align everything after the first EX Skill. Layout buttons such as 3-turn EX · Passive Def · Earliest first EX return to the plan from just before you turned them on when clicked again.
guide.section.turnPlan.title: Per-turn Action Plan
guide.section.ultMode.body: The second tab of Advanced Action Setup. Choose per companion whether to use the EX Skill on planned turns (Planned turns), only on those turns (Planned turns only), or as soon as it is ready (As soon as ready). The top of the tab lists what decides the EX Skill, in priority order (timeline → sync → policy → extra actions). The companion window shows a summary of the current policy, and the button next to it opens this tab directly.
guide.section.ultMode.note: When the guild altar’s ‘chance to cut the CD on action · on EX Skill’ effects are on, a notice appears at the top of the tab and each companion gets an ‘Assume chance cooldown cuts succeed’ switch. With it on, just enough cooldown cuts are counted as successful on the EX Skill turns set by your plan or sync, so you can plan EX Skills on turns the base cooldown cannot reach (e.g. turns 3·6·9·12 for a 3-turn cooldown). The result header also shows how likely that exact flow is. To see the real odds, use ‘As soon as ready’. The ‘Earliest first EX’ button in the companion window’s per-turn plan puts the first EX Skill on the earliest possible turn and fills the rest with the normal cooldown cycle.
